feedback: If a learner thinks the five-10p set is 'more' than a single 50p because it has more coins, count the VALUE of each set to the same total and show that more coins can equal fewer coins in value.
Prompt: 'You made 30p with three 10p. Can you make 30p using a 20p? What else do you need?' to rehearse swap reasoning.
Reinforce that the swap did not change the amount, only the coins used.
activities.intendedInsight: Exchanging one coin for equivalent smaller coins keeps the total fixed, so a set with more coins can be worth exactly the same as a set with fewer coins.
learnerActions: Start with one way of making the total (e.g. a single 50p).
Swap one coin for equivalent smaller coins — lift the 50p and replace it with two 20p and a 10p — and check the total is unchanged.
Try other swaps (e.g. 30p made as three 10p; swap to 20p + 10p) and confirm each keeps the same value.
Describe in words why the new set equals the old one: the coin values still sum to the same amount.
activities.title: Swap a coin for equivalent smaller coins without changing the total

feedback: If a learner accepts a set that relies on a non-existent 8p coin, point out there is no 8p coin and ask which real coins could make that value.
If a set is wrongly rejected, re-count its value to the total together.
activities.intendedInsight: Checking whether a coin set reaches a stated total, and rejecting sets that use invented coins, reinforces that value is what matters and that only real denominations may be used.
learnerActions: Decide which of several coin sets make a given total (e.g. 'which of these make 50p?').
Sort sets into 'makes 50p' and 'does not make 50p'.
Match a total to a valid coin set.
Spot and reject any set that relies on a non-existent coin, such as an invented 8p.
activities.title: Sort and match coin sets to totals (recognition practice)

feedback: If the learner stops after one way, prompt 'Is there another way to make 50p?' and keep a shared list of ways found.
Ask 'Could you make 50p with an 8p coin? Why not?' to surface the real-denominations constraint.
activities.intendedInsight: Explaining and justifying equal-value combinations aloud rehearses the reasoning and the language of 'same total, different coins'.
learnerActions: Respond to a shopkeeper asking 'Can you pay 50p a different way?' by naming or laying out another valid coin set.
Explain aloud why the new way is worth the same as the first.
Be challenged to find yet another way, and, when only a few coin types are allowed (e.g. 10p, 20p and 50p), to say how you could be sure you've found them all.
activities.title: Pay a different way — shopkeeper talk (optional spoken extension)
